job.style: a clear textbook explanation with one worked example

response.passage: Geometry helps us understand the shapes around us by measuring their properties. An angle is formed when two rays meet at a common point called the vertex. The size of an angle depends only on the amount of rotation between its arms, not on the length of the arms themselves. For instance, if you have a small angle and a large angle with very long arms, the angle size remains unchanged by the arm length. When measuring an angle with a protractor, you must place the centre of the protractor exactly on the vertex and align the baseline with one arm. A straight line is actually a special angle measuring exactly 180 degrees. Furthermore, triangles are classified by their sides; an isosceles triangle has at least two equal sides, regardless of how close the third side is in length. Finally, a square is a special type of rectangle because it possesses all the properties of a rectangle, such as having four right angles and opposite sides that are equal. Understanding these definitions prevents common errors in geometry. For example, if you see a triangle with sides of 5cm, 5cm, and 6cm, it is isosceles because two sides are equal, even though the third side is nearly the same length.
response.summary: This passage explains how to correctly measure angles and classify triangles based on their properties. It clarifies that arm length does not affect angle size and defines squares as a specific type of rectangle.
